To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the heterogeneous reaction between CrVI and FeII in carbonate GR is fast, (ii) the reduction of aqueous CrVI is accompanied by the oxidation of lattice Fe II to Fe III, and (iii) the formation of Cr III monolayers at GR surface induces a progressive rate limitation.

the heterogeneous reaction between CrVI and FeII in carbonate (FeII) green rust results in the formation of successive monolayers of CrIII at the surface of green rust particles and in progressive rate limitations due to the passivation effect.
the heterogeneous reaction between CrVI and FeII in carbonate GR is kinetically controlled by the formation of successive layers of CrIII precipitates at the surface of green rust particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a mechanistic understanding of the heterogeneous reaction between aqueous CrVI and FeII in carbonate GR, and with the determination of the kinetics of the reaction and of its rate limitations.
the kinetics and mechanism of the reduction of aqueous CrVI by green rusts.
the development of a model for the reduction of aqueous CrVI by Fe(II) in carbonate green rust, and the determination of the kinetics and mechanisms of this heterogeneous reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the efficiency of green rust for CrVI removal is not as high as it is for As(V) or Se(IV) removal.
the reduction of CrVI by FeII in carbonate GR is an effective process, but the efficiency is progressively limited with the formation of successive layers of CrIII precipitates.
